about:
Icon Modern was founded in 2007 by Rocky Levy and Aaron Tvrdy in Chicago, Illinois. What began as a side project diverting urban trees destined for landfill into handcrafted furniture has grown into a full-service custom fabrication company operating from a 10,000-square-foot office and showroom in the city's West Loop neighborhood. The founders, who met through a shared passion for sustainable design, started in a garage and quickly secured projects with national brands such as Starbucks, Whole Foods, and Twitter.

The company produces commercial furniture and architectural elements — conference tables, community tables, reception desks, space dividers, ceiling elements, feature walls, planters, and countertops — using a broad range of materials including urban hardwoods, steel, stone, glass, and veneers. In-house capabilities span CNC machining, metal fabrication and welding, woodworking, powder coating, stone and glass fabrication, as well as engineering, value engineering, 3D rendering, shop drawings, and prototyping. Icon Modern imposes no minimum or maximum order quantities and emphasizes shorter lead times through a streamlined process.

The firm serves architects, interior designers, and corporate clients across hospitality, retail, technology, and corporate office sectors. Notable projects include installations for Caterpillar, Jump Trading, and IPG, alongside the earlier brand-name work. A dedicated project manager oversees each job from concept through installation, handling engineering, detailing, and logistics on the client's behalf.

Icon Modern's founding mission centers on sustainability and creative reuse: sourcing all materials within a 100-mile radius of its Chicago shop and giving urban trees a second life as furniture. The team, which includes architects and designers, aims to make custom fabrication more accessible to designers by offering a wider material palette and a collaborative, end-to-end service that eliminates the need for clients to coordinate multiple vendors.
